typed_core.name: document_title
typed_core.why: identity/classification — distinguishes an income LOE from other LOE subtypes for human review

typed_core.name: letter_date
typed_core.why: identity — when written; recency of the explanation (processor)

typed_core.name: borrower_name
typed_core.why: identity — whose LOE (flattened from borrower_names person[])

typed_core.name: borrower_name_2
typed_core.why: identity — co-borrower when the letter is joint

typed_core.name: borrower_names_raw
typed_core.why: disambiguator — verbatim signer string so a bad name split stays visible

typed_core.name: issuer_name
typed_core.why: identity/source — normally the borrower; confirms the letter is borrower-authored, not third-party
typed_core.prompt_hint: The issuer of a LOE is normally the borrower, not a third party — do not expect institutional letterhead

typed_core.name: employer_business_or_income_source
typed_core.why: identity — which income stream this letter explains; attaches the LOE to a paystub/VOE (processor)

typed_core.name: position_or_income_type
typed_core.why: disambiguator — which role/income when a borrower has several sources (processor)

typed_core.name: income_issue_type
typed_core.why: identity/classification; what is being explained (gap, decline, bonus, new job)

typed_core.name: affected_dates_or_period
typed_core.why: identity; the period the explanation covers (processor)

typed_core.name: reason_or_cause

typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the reason verbatim; do not summarize or infer a cause the borrower did not state

typed_core.name: return_to_work_or_start_date
typed_core.why: processor — forward-looking date supporting income continuity; cheap future rule

typed_core.name: current_employment_orincome_status
typed_core.why: processor; is the income still active

typed_core.name: income_continuance_expectation
typed_core.why: processor — borrower's stated expectation of continuance

typed_core.name: variable_income_or_one_time_payment_classification
typed_core.why: disambiguator — whether the amount recurs or is one-time (processor)

typed_core.name: employment_gap_or_leave_details
typed_core.why: processor — gap/leave specifics when present

typed_core.name: supporting_documents_summary
typed_core.why: processor — what evidence the borrower references (flattened; see Open questions)

typed_core.name: borrower_certification
typed_core.why: processor — presence/wording of the truthfulness attestation

typed_core.name: signature_date
typed_core.why: execution — date the borrower signed (flattened from borrower_signatures_and_dates signature[])

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: identity linkage (flattened) — ties the letter to the subject file when stated

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity linkage — ties the letter to the loan file when stated

rejected.name: form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: a borrower LOE is not a standardized form

rejected.name: issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: no consumer; issuer is the borrower

rejected.name: effective_date, expiration_date, statement_period_start/end

rejected.name: party_names, party_addresses
rejected.reason: duplicate borrower_names; no rule addresses parties individually

rejected.name: account_case_reference_number
rejected.reason: no consumer on a borrower letter

rejected.name: notary_block, signature_blocks
rejected.reason: a LOE is not notarized; borrower signature captured flat

rejected.name: document_status_or_version
rejected.reason: no draft/final lifecycle for a borrower letter

rejected.name: income_amounts_orvariance
rejected.reason: itemized amounts have no rule; catch-all captures them

encoding_variations: income_issue_type / current_employment_orincome_status are catalog enum with enum_values: null — issuers use free prose ('still employed', 'on leave', 'returned'). Degrade to str; the model must not be forced into a fixed vocabulary.
affected_dates_or_period is a date_range with no coercer — issuers write 'March–June 2025', 'Q2 2025', or '3 months' — keep the verbatim string.
Borrower name may appear in the letterhead, the body, and the signature line with different formatting — borrower_names_raw preserves the signature form.

open_questions.recommendation: (a) flat str — usually a short phrase, no consumer; leave until a rule needs to match named attachments
leave to the catch-all; flag for review if underwriting later wants itemized before/after figures typed
joint LOEs may sign two names on one line; borrower_names_raw retained so the tag layer can judge a bad split

notes: This document carries no rules in the packet, so there is no rule floor. Every typed-core field is justified by identity, disambiguation, or processor review. A borrower-authored narrative letter is mostly free prose; the typed core captures who/what/when so the letter can be attached to a borrower and income source, and the narrative itself falls to the catch-all.

loan_number is confidential in the catalog but is treated as an identity/linkage field (consistent with the standard's handling), not registered in _PII_FIELDS. No SSN, DOB, or account number appears on this document type.

Ambiguity: signature_date is described as 'execution' in the markdown, which is not one of the five reason_class values; classified as processor (a signing date the processor reviews for recency/validity) as best guess.
